# Appeal of Denial – Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-19
**Member:** Rowan Carter
**Member ID:** W914903090
**Reference Number:** POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Missouri
**Governing Policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html), last review 02/26/2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which I received in a notice dated 2026-08-19. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I believe the record shows that I meet the plan's own published criteria for a unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. I am asking Aetna to reconsider this decision.

## Why I meet the plan's criteria

**1. My condition affects a single compartment, which the plan's policy identifies as an indication for UKA rather than TKA.**

The policy states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My MRI from 2026-06-09 shows full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment only, with a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 4 medially. The record does not describe involvement of the lateral or patellofemoral compartments. This is consistent with the single-compartment indication described in the policy.

The policy further states that UKA:

> "is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria (see also Additional Note ):"

My imaging findings and exam (positive provocative testing, pain-limited range of motion) document advanced osteoarthritis limited to the medial compartment.

**2. I completed a documented course of conservative therapy.**

The policy requires:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My physical therapy discharge note documents 14 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-17), focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. Together, this treatment meets or exceeds the 12-week non-surgical treatment period described in the policy, with more than half of that time consisting of formal, in-person physical therapy.

**3. The severity of my condition supports moving forward with surgery.**

The policy notes:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral) or severe angular deformity, or for avascular necrosis with collapse of tibial or femoral condyle, or progressive flexion contracture."

My MRI documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial, weight-bearing compartment. My symptoms have progressed over 9 months and now include nightly pain that wakes me 3-4 times, and an inability to climb stairs without assistance.

**4. Regarding the injection-timing consideration in the policy.**

I note that the policy lists a corticosteroid injection given "within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty" as a factor bearing on medical necessity. My injection was administered on 2026-06-17. I ask the plan to confirm, based on the surgery date proposed by Dr. Marchetti, whether this falls outside that 12-week window. [Placeholder: scheduled or proposed surgery date, if not already in the record.]

**5. No absolute contraindication is documented.**

My chart shows no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. I am not aware of any finding in my record that matches an absolute contraindication under the policy.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Aetna to reverse this denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) recommended by Dr. Marchetti, based on the documentation summarized above. If any additional records are needed from my surgeon's office to complete this review, please let me know what is missing so it can be provided promptly.

I understand my appeal must be received by the deadline stated in my denial letter, which I am treating as 2027-02-15. I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form through my account at aetna.com, and/or by fax to 859-425-3379, and I am confirming the correct appeal address printed on my denial letter before mailing any paper copy.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Rowan Carter
Member ID: W914903090
